scope: Warm native input through local HTTP/MCP and resident Swift, with compact AX result checks and independent browser DOM/AppKit action receipts. Excludes model inference, initial frame, and fixture startup. No input replay after mismatch.
notes: 800 initial single-click trials and 1000 lower-hold trials passed across Chrome and AppKit; explicit double/triple clicks also passed. Zero hold means no deliberate delay, not zero event-delivery latency.

The user reported moving the mouse after the first 16 ms path / 32 ms release trial. That failure is potentially interfered with. Retests of 16/32 and 32/16 also failed; these settings were not selected.
Initial AppKit startup OCR read 0 as O. The harness now accepts the ambiguous glyph for locating the counter and still verifies the exact native AX value. No click was sent in that startup failure.

The first drag sweep accumulated per-step scheduling delays. Later runs use absolute deadlines and an independently controlled destination dwell. Do not compare requested duration alone across those implementations.

Two runs of the selected 32 ms path / 32 ms release profile each verified all 100 drops and drag-end releases. This is evidence for the controlled HTML5 drag fixture, not a guarantee for arbitrary applications or Finder-to-browser file transfers.
The 24 fps budget is 41.667 ms per whole cycle. Zero-hold click medians approach/exceed that rate; tails and complete drop acknowledgement remain slower.
